s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute neurological deterioration with impaired extraocular movement, tetraparesis, and signs of meningeal irritation
salient_findings: Mild sinking of the right leg
key_facts: 10-year history of treatment with various medications
No history of severe lymphocytopenia
Impaired extraocular movement at last outpatient visit
Mild sinking of the right leg at position test
Developed dizziness and nausea a few months later
Received methylprednisolone treatment
Presented with moderate tetraparesis, headache, fever, and neck stiffness
Family members had fever, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, recovering within 3 days
Patient had mild gastrointestinal symptoms prior to neurological symptoms
Positive Romberg test
Initial white blood cell count: 4900/μL
Lymphocyte count: 1240/μL
Later white blood cell count: 18,000/μL
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed increased protein level and 108 cells/mL
Cerebrospinal fluid culture was positive
MRI showed hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum with slight contrast enhancement
